newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss lower house passes telecom reform bill.
newsitem.headline: Swiss lower house passes telecom reform bill.

text.p: Switzerland's lower house of parliament on Wednesday approved a reform of the Swiss postal and telecommunications market, including a partial privatisation of the telecommunications activities.
The lower house approved the government's proposal from June this year, which splits the postal and telecommunications authority into two seperate units.
While the telecommunications' activities will be transformed into a joint stock company with the Swiss government holding a majority, the postal authority will remain a state-owned agency.
The goal is to sell a minority stake in Swiss Telecom.
The reform is scheduled to take effect on January 1, 1998, in line with the European Union's liberalisation of its telecommuncations market.
Full privatisation of Swiss Telecom had not been planned because this would have required a change to the Swiss constitution, a very lengthy process.
Switzerland took a first step to loosening its telecommunications law in 1991, allowing private companies to offer some kinds of data transmission.
But Telecom still holds a monopoly over most voice transmission and the cellular phone network.
